name: crontab
plain: cron runs commands on a schedule: every minute, every night at 02:00, at every reboot. `crontab` is the command that edits your personal schedule.
Each line has five time fields and then a command: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week. A star * means every.
For security work it matters twice: persistence (an attacker adds a job) and privilege escalation (a root cron job runs a script that you can write to).

Every / list / range / step. */10 means every 10.
System-wide schedules; /etc/crontab and /etc/cron.d need a user field.

mistakes: Cron has a tiny PATH: use full paths to every program.
Forgetting 2>&1 and a log, so errors vanish.
Using % in a command without escaping it as \%.
Editing /etc/crontab and leaving out the user column.
Wiping a crontab with crontab -r when you meant -e.
